plan.title: Paired control-vs-treated DE + pathway analysis (n=5 subjects)
plan.analytical_narrative: Five subjects each contribute a paired control and treated blood sample (STAR/featureCounts raw counts, 12000 genes x 10 samples). The paired within-subject design calls for a DESeq2 model with subject as a blocking term (~subject + condition) so that inter-subject variability is removed and the treatment effect is estimated within each subject, per the paired-design rule from the knowledge service. The pipeline runs standard sample-structure QC, minimal pre-filtering, DESeq2 normalization and Wald testing with subject-blocked design, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change, BH-adjusted significance calling with independent filtering, and downstream pathway interpretation. Given only 5 pairs (n<50 typically expected to pass FDR<0.05 in blood), the enrichment plan uses fgsea preranked GSEA on the full ranked gene list against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, staged locally) as the first pass and Reactome/WikiPathways as follow-up collections, per the knowledge service's enrichment guidance (rule R-0048) rather than over-representation analysis, which needs a sizeable significant gene list to have power. A GO-BP over-representation pass with clusterProfiler + rrvgo term reduction is included as a secondary, discrete-list-based method for robustness if the significant gene count is adequate, and edgeR quasi-likelihood is run in parallel to DESeq2 as the second method for a robustness overlap check per rule R-0042. Every reference used (MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways human GMTs; org.Hs.eg.db) is confirmed present in the environment before use.
